summary: fabtoolkit ships a reverse-shell backdoor and remote-config-driven RCE/exfil
details: fabtoolkit 0.1.1 embeds a remote-controlled implant that is reachable via `selftest()` and `python -m fabtoolkit`. A child process forks a detached daemon (`os.fork` + `setsid`) that fetches a JSON config from https://transfer.archivete.am/H2Uxm/fabdeploycheck-config.json over an HTTPS connection with TLS verification disabled (`ssl._create_unverified_context`), then dispatches operator-chosen actions: `run` executes arbitrary argv via `subprocess.run`; `file` reads attacker-specified filesystem paths (with environment-variable expansion, so paths like `~/.aws`, `~/.ssh`, and arbitrary secrets are reachable), zips the collected contents, and PUTs them to the anonymous file host transfer.archivete.am under an operator-chosen name; `tcp` and `http` perform further operator-directed network I/O; and `revsh` activates a reverse-shell loop that repeatedly fetches `<base>/<ident>-cmd.txt`, executes the returned bytes via `/bin/sh -c`, and PUTs stdout/stderr back to the same host. Before launching the shell loop, the daemon enumerates `/proc/*/cmdline` and `SIGKILL`s any process whose cmdline contains `FABDRV3`, `fabdrv2`, or `connection ready`, removing prior implant instances to keep a single live backdoor. The destination host, the TLS-verification bypass, the detached-daemon persistence pattern, and the process-cleanup cmdline tokens all demonstrate operational malware rather than a developer tool.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
